verdict.rationale: ByteAsk documents its own debugging workflow. It joins a running gdb session through a bridge and reads live state, drives sanitizers and the test suite, and returns raw reports with frames, files and line numbers intact. It also takes conversational input via messages into a session. The natural-language querying side of troubleshooting is only implied by the conversational agent design, not explicitly documented, and all evidence is vendor-claimed. missing for 10: explicit documentation of asking debugging questions in natural language (e.g. 'why does this crash?'), worked troubleshooting examples, independent or hands-on corroboration of debugging quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug issues and troubleshoot using natural-language queries

citations.quote: ByteAsk joins through a bridge you start in your gdb, reads the live state, and asks before it changes anything.
It hands back the raw report with the frames, files and line numbers intact, so you can check the agent's reasoning against the same evidence.
drives the real toolchain - sanitizers, your test suite, and any gdb session you already have open - and hands you a diff that survived the debugger.
A read-only run can still build your program under AddressSanitizer and run it.
sends a message into a running session from another terminal.
